observations.series_5: All three selected sagittal slices are markedly dark under full-volume display. Header and percentile windows increase anatomical visibility but also reveal strong grain and reduced fine structure separation. The effect exists at native resolution and cannot be attributed entirely to cache downsampling or full-scale darkness. No acquisition cause is identified.
observations.series_6: All three selected coronal slices retain broad structure and contours, with pronounced superior-to-inferior signal nonuniformity; the inferior region is much brighter while the upper region remains dark or grainy. Header and percentile windows brighten the image but do not remove that distribution. This is visible natively and in cache.
observations.series_11: The three selected coronal slices have clearer internal structure separation and more even signal across the joint than series 6 in the compared fields. Some inferior darkening remains. Cache images soften fine detail while preserving gross contours.
observations.series_12: The three selected sagittal slices show substantially clearer internal structure separation than series 5 under both the original display and native alternative windows. No corresponding severe global grain obscures the anatomy in these sampled panels.
